title: Three accounts, read in francs
subtitle: What the franc’s move did to three accounts
note: Antevo's model book: one household that spends in francs, three accounts named Capital Preservation, Balanced and Growth, nine securities, all but one priced in dollars. Figures are shares of the whole from Antevo engine answers on the date shown; holdings are described, not named.

tries.label: The book, currency by currency
tries.source: Antevo Wealth, Research and Executive Brief, 25 Nov 2026. Currencies from the price currency of each holding; one dollar bought 0.8342 francs on 25 November.

items.name: The currencies
evidence: 85.9% of the book priced in dollars, 14.1% in francs, none in euros
The only franc holding is the Swiss food maker, held in all three accounts

items.name: This week
evidence: The dollar lost 1.5% against the franc over the week to 25 November
On 85.9% of the book, that is about 1.3% off its value in francs from the currency alone

items.name: This year
evidence: The dollar is 3.4% up on the franc over the year, 0.8% over the month
Over the year the currency added about 2.9% to the book in francs

items.name: The steady part
evidence: A short-dated US government bond fund is 15.4% of the book
It is 32.5% of the Capital Preservation account, the largest position in it, and its value in francs moves with the dollar

items.name: Each account
evidence: Capital Preservation 78.6% in dollars, Balanced 84.8%, Growth 93.4%
Every 1% the dollar moves against the franc moves the book about 0.86% in francs, before any move in the shares

items.why: Capital Preservation carries the bond fund that moves with the dollar; Growth is 93.4% in dollars.

items.do: Ask your bank whether any fund you hold is a currency-hedged share class
items.why: The record shows the price currency of each fund, not whether it is hedged; only the fund’s papers say that.

items.do: Read gains and losses in both currencies
items.why: Over the year the dollar added about 2.9% to the book in francs; this week it took about 1.3% back.
US inflation on 25 November, US jobs figures on 4 December, the Swiss National Bank on 10 December.

sections.title: Why the franc rose this week
sections.so_what: The franc tends to rise when shares fall, so a dollar book can lose twice in a sell-off: on the shares and on the currency.
evidence: The franc rose as AI shares sold off; a gauge of share-market fear climbed above 30 on 24 November
The desk reads it as money seeking safety, not new Swiss data
One dollar bought 0.8342 francs on 25 November, down 1.5% in a week

sections.title: What held the dollar up this year
sections.so_what: The year’s currency gain came from the gap between US and Swiss rates; anything that narrows the gap works against it.
evidence: US interest rates sit far above Swiss rates, which are at 0%
That gap pulled money into dollars through most of the year: the dollar is 3.4% up on the franc over twelve months

sections.title: Swiss prices and the Swiss National Bank
sections.so_what: A Swiss rate rise would narrow the gap that has supported the dollar behind 85.9% of the book.
evidence: Swiss inflation rose to 1.5% in October, its core about 0.5%
The Swiss National Bank holds at 0% and decides on 10 December

sections.title: The dates ahead
sections.so_what: All three bear on the rate gap, and with it on the book’s value in francs.
evidence: 25 November: US core inflation for October; above 3.2% would restore bets on a US rate rise in December
4 December: US jobs figures for November
10 December: the Swiss National Bank

links.text: The book is 85.9% in dollars and the desk sees the dollar 1.5% weaker on the week: about 1.3% off the book in francs, on top of whatever the shares did.
The Capital Preservation account’s largest position is a US government bond fund. The desk’s flight to safety lifted the franc, so the part meant to be steady moved with the currency.
The desk explains the year by the rate gap; the brief’s dates, US inflation, US jobs and the Swiss decision, are the events that move it.

watch: US core inflation for October, 25 November
US jobs figures for November, 4 December
Swiss inflation and the Swiss National Bank’s decision, 10 December
Share-market fear: the franc rose as it climbed
disclaimer: From Antevo answers, each dated. The effect of the currency is arithmetic on today's holdings, not a forecast. Describing a book is not advice: nothing here says what to buy, sell, hold or hedge.
